author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts health officials announced the state's eighth human case of West Nile virus this year on Sept. 18. The patient is a woman in her 30s who was exposed in an area of Middlesex County where other exposures have occurred, according to the Department of Public Health.

Seven of the eight cases have been linked to areas of Middlesex and Suffolk counties classified as high risk. DPH lists Boston, Brookline, Cambridge, Chelsea, Everett, Malden, Newton, Revere, Somerville, Watertown and Winthrop at high risk, while most of the rest of the state remains at moderate risk.

State surveillance has found 327 West Nile-positive mosquito samples in 13 counties this season. Eastern equine encephalitis has also been detected in 21 mosquito samples, but DPH said there have been no human or animal EEE cases this year.

Officials recommend EPA-registered repellent, protective clothing, repaired window screens and removing standing water. Residents in higher-risk areas should consider limiting outdoor activity from dusk to dawn, when mosquitoes are most active.
dek: A woman in her 30s was exposed in Middlesex County as state officials report eight human cases and high-risk communities around Boston.
headline: Massachusetts reports eighth human West Nile case of 2026
